title: CS2 World Bundle district record (contract section 8d)
description: One line of districts.jsonl (JSON Lines): a player-drawn district polygon and the name the player typed on it. THIS IS THE ONLY SOURCE OF PLACE NAMES IN A CS2 CITY — a network segment's attrs.name is a STREET and a building's attrs.brand is a BUSINESS, and neither answers 'where in the city am I'. A district is an area entity with the same Game.Areas Node/Triangle grid buffers as section 8b's surfaces, but it paints nothing and is never rendered, which is why it is a layer of its own rather than a kind inside areas.jsonl (that layer's query demands Game.Areas.Surface). The name comes from the game's own NameSystem.GetRenderedLabelName, the same call the vanilla vector export makes. A city with no districts drawn ships an empty file, not a missing layer.

id.description: Producer-local unique identifier (the ECS entity index).

name.description: The district's rendered label — what the player typed, or the game's generated default. MAY BE EMPTY: a district whose name the name system cannot resolve ships an empty string rather than being dropped, and the rip report counts them, so a consumer never has to guess whether an absent name means an absent district.

nodes.description: The polygon's corners as bundle-frame world positions (section 2.1) — NOT mesh-frame mirrored. At least 3.

triangles.description: The game's own triangulation: index triplets into this record's own 'nodes'. Identical encoding to section 8b.

centroid.description: The mean of 'nodes', in the bundle frame. Free to carry and it is what most consumers actually want: a consumer placing one marker per district (a fast-travel point, a map label) never has to triangulate the polygon. It is the node mean and NOT the area centroid, so a district with an uneven node distribution has it pulled toward the denser side; use the triangles when that matters.
